prompt: Two images are provided. The first gives the crane's pose, angle, placement and scale only. The second is a painting of a standing crane: it gives the brush hand. Paint the flying crane again by the same painter, with the same large soft brush, the same sumi ink and the same warm rice paper as the standing crane: a bold freehand sumi-e painting made in few strokes. One red-crowned crane in flight, both wings raised high in an upstroke, the long neck stretched forward to the right, beak pointing right, legs trailing straight behind and slightly down. Anatomically correct: exactly two wings, two thin legs with small feet, one head, one long beak. The black neck is one loaded, wet, jet-black calligraphic stroke. The black flight feathers along the back edge of each wing are broad, heavy, jet-black strokes laid side by side, ending in split dry-brush tips. The white wings and body are bare unpainted paper, held by a confident contour line that swells and thins and breaks like calligraphy, with only two or three broad pale grey wet wash strokes. Each leg is one quick thin dark stroke. The small crown on top of the head is a tiny touch of gold leaf, never red. No fine feather detail, no stippling, no hatching, no pencil line, no thin even outline, not a soft watercolour illustration. The whole bird inside the frame with clear empty paper margins on every side and nothing cut off. Plain empty warm rice paper ground, evenly lit. No reeds, no water, no mountains, no mist, no sun, no text, no seal, no signature, no border. Nothing red anywhere.
